1,000 filings in the current training table, in table order.
Each block is one 10-K. Each numbered line is the opening sentence of one Item 1A paragraph.
Opening lines shorter than 8 words, longer than 42 words, at least 12 percent digits,
or matching the risk-factor legend are left out.
A sentence marked with * is one of the sentences kept in the model text (at most 10).

  2. We have incurred significant losses since our founding and anticipate that we will continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future and may never achieve or maintain profitability.

  3. We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company and have not yet generated revenues from product sales.

  4. We have devoted most of our financial resources to research and development, including preclinical and clinical development of product candidates.

  5. The net losses we incur may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and year to year, such that a period-to-period comparison of our results of operations may not be a good indication of our future performance.

  6. Our profitability depends on our ability to develop and commercialize our current and future product candidates.

  7. To become and remain profitable, we must succeed in developing and eventually commercializing products that generate significant revenue.

  8. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future.

  14. seek to discover and develop additional product candidates;

  19. Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with pharmaceutical product development, we are unable to accurately predict the timing or amount of increased expenses or when, or if, we will be able to achieve profitability.

  20. Even if we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis.

  21. Future conditions might require us to make substantial write-downs in our assets, which would adversely affect our balance sheet and results of operations.

  22. We review our long-lived tangible and intangible assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value of an asset may not be recoverable.

  23. Our ability to continue as a going concern will require us to obtain additional financing to fund our current operations, which may be unavailable on acceptable terms, or at all.

  24. Our recurring operating losses and current operating plans raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.

  25. We will require substantial additional financing to achieve our goals, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed would force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development or commercialization efforts.

  1. In addition to risks and uncertainties in the ordinary course of business that are common to all businesses, important factors that are specific to our industry and us could materially affect our future performance and results.

  2. Our business is sensitive to economic conditions that may affect consumer confidence, consumer discretionary spending, or our access to credit in a manner that adversely affects our operations.

  3. Economic trends can affect consumer confidence and consumers’ discretionary spending:

  4. Negative economic conditions and the persistence of elevated levels of unemployment can affect consumers’ disposable incomes and, therefore, affect the demand for entertainment and leisure activities.

  5. Declines in the residential real estate market, increases in individual tax rates and other factors that we cannot accurately predict may reduce the disposable income of our customers.

  6. Decreases in consumer discretionary spending could affect us even if these decreases occur in other markets.

  7. Lower consumer confidence or reductions in consumer discretionary spending could result in fewer patrons spending money at our racetrack.

  8. Forces beyond our control could affect our business.

  9. Consumer demand for card casino and racetrack properties such as ours is particularly sensitive to downturns in the economy and the associated effect on discretionary spending on leisure activities.

  10. We face significant competition, both directly from other racing and gaming operations and indirectly from other forms of entertainment and leisure time activities, which could have a material adverse effect on our operations.

  11. We face intense competition in our market, particularly competition from NMHI, which offers unbanked card games similar to those we offer.

  12. We expect competition for our existing and future operations to increase from NMHI, existing tribal casinos, and racetracks that are able to subsidize their purses with alternative gaming revenues.

  13. A lack of confidence in the integrity of our core businesses could affect our ability to retain our customers and engage with new customers.

* 14. The integrity of horseracing, casino gaming, and pari-mutuel wagering industries must be perceived as fair to patrons and the public at large.

* 15. Nationally the popularity of horse racing has declined.
